script: Now that the Kawhi Leonard Clippers era is officially over, and looking back at it, this might be one of the worst win-now failures in NBA history. Kawhi spent seven seasons with the Clippers. From 2019 to 2026. Leonard on the Clippers: 7 seasons, 5 postseason, 3 series wins, 1 Western Conference Finals, 0 finals. Since the postseason experiences were underwhelming, they won just three playoff series in seven years. Their deepest run came in 2021 when the Clippers reached their first Western Conference Finals in franchise history. Which isn't a big deal, but Kawhi didn't even play in that series because he tore his ACL against Utah, meaning Kawhi himself never played past the second round as a Clipper. Compare that to his time in Toronto, where in just one single season in 2019, Kawhi won four playoff series and an NBA championship. Remember what the Clippers gave up to build this team? They traded Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and a massive amount of picks for Paul George. So Kawhi would stay there. The Clippers were consistently good, but injuries kept destroying their championship chances. So after seven seasons with just five playoff appearances, three series wins, one conference finals appearance, no NBA finals and no championships. And now the Kawhi era is going back to Toronto. The Clippers are technically younger and trying to retool, but considering expectations and everything that they lost after the scandal, I think you have to call this Kawhi Clippers era a failure.
